claim.text: On the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2021 Task 1a data, the procedure requires only one or two pruning-search iterations ($T=1$ or $2$) to find high-quality low-complexity models.

Among three evaluated Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) mask-selection strategies—(i) large-final, (ii) small-weights, and (iii) global small-weights—the small-weights masking strategy was empirically selected, as claim 3 states.

The small-weights masking strategy produced a superior trade-off between classification accuracy and compression rate on the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2021 Task 1a validation experiments.

The iterative Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) pruning search procedure, as described in note 1, applied to Inception-based student architectures yields sparse subnetworks that retain or modestly change validation predictive metrics compared to their unpruned seeds while achieving very large parameter reduction.

Visualization and empirical examples demonstrate that discovered models, as described in claim 4, have sparsity corresponding to up to a 149× compression rate in the examined shallow Inception student model.

An ensemble built from pruned and distilled Large Inception (LIC) and Shallow Inception (SIC) models under the Acoustic Lottery pipeline achieved a validation accuracy of 79.4% and a log loss of 0.640 on the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2021 Task 1a development set.
The integrated compression-and-training workflow can reach high predictive performance comparable to much larger prior systems while using compressed components.

An ensemble composed of pruned and distilled Large Inception (LIC) models produced a system with 117 KB non-zero parameters, validation accuracy $78.7\%$, and log loss $0.644$ on the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2021 Task 1a development set.

The Acoustic Lottery approach can produce multi-device-robust acoustic scene classification (ASC) systems meeting the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) Task 1a size constraint.

Applying teacher-student learning (TSL) to the Shallow Inception (SIC) student model improved validation accuracy from 67.8% to 68.9% and reduced log loss from 0.954 to 0.919 on the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2021 development set
Distillation of a large two-stage teacher into a small student increases the student model's predictive performance under acoustic scene classification (ASC) multi-device conditions.

Post-training dynamic range quantization (DRQ), that statically quantizes weights to 8-bit integers and dynamically quantizes activations, reduces model file size by roughly a factor of four versus 32-bit storage.

when applied after Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) pruning and teacher-student learning (TSL), this quantization produced a Large Inception (LIC)-based system with 103 KB non-zero-parameter size, validation accuracy $78.2\%$, and log loss $0.723$ on the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2021 Task 1a development set,
Post-training dynamic range quantization (DRQ) can be used in concert with sparse-subnetwork discovery to reach stringent size budgets.

Empirically on the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2021 Task 1a data, the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) pruning search—which repeatedly trains the model via teacher-student learning, prunes by masking weights, and resets surviving weights to their initial random values—required only $T=1$ or $T=2$ pruning-search iterations to find high-quality low-complexity acoustic models that do not suffer significant validation accuracy degradation compared to their high-complexity teachers.

note.text: elaboration of iterative Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) pruning search procedure: —which, starting from a seed network $G_0$ with random initialization $\Theta_0$, repeats for $T$ iterations: train via teacher-student learning on augmented data to obtain weights $\Theta_t$, then if $t<T$ compute a binary mask on $\Theta_t$ to obtain a pruned subgraph $G_p$ from $G_0$, load the homologous subset of initial weights $\Theta_p \subset \Theta_0$ corresponding to surviving parameters, and set the next model $G_{t+1}=G_p(\Theta_p)$; output the trained pruned model $G_T(\Theta_T)$—
